transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi... um, well, I guess I'm here because things have just been really, really hard lately, especially at the salon. I'm a cosmetologist, I do hair mostly, and usually I'm so quick, you know? Like, I can get a client in and out—wash, cut, blow-dry, boom, onto the next one. I've always prided myself on my timing. But lately... I don't even know how to explain it, it's like... my hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work. 

It's so frustrating because my brain knows what I'm supposed to do, but my body just won't do it at the normal speed. Like, even just sectioning hair—which is literally the most basic thing, you just take the tail comb and part it out—or mixing color in the back room... it takes me forever now. I'll just be standing there with the color bowl and the developer, and it's like I'm moving in slow motion and I can't snap out of it. And it's not just me overthinking it, either, because people have actually started noticing that I’m just slower than I used to be. 

My manager pulled me aside the other day and asked if I was feeling okay because my appointment times are dragging out, and my clients are sitting in the chair way longer than they should be for just a partial highlight or a root touch-up. I couldn't even give her a good answer because I don't know why I'm moving like this. It's just this heavy, dragging feeling in my arms and hands, and it's really messing up my schedule and making me so stressed out because in this industry, time is literally money, and if I can't keep up my pace... I don't know, it's just really scaring me that I can't seem to physically speed up no matter how hard I try.
Do you experience this slowness or heaviness in your arms and hands outside of work, like when you're doing everyday activities at home?

Um... well, it's not just at the salon, no. It's... it's kind of everywhere now, honestly. Like, even just waking up in the morning, right? Usually, I'm the kind of person who hears the alarm, hits snooze maybe once, and then I'm up, making coffee, getting ready for the day. But now, just the act of pushing the blankets off... it feels like they weigh a hundred pounds. And then when I finally do get up, getting dressed is a whole ordeal. 

I'll just stand in front of my closet staring at my clothes, and when I finally reach out to grab a shirt off a hanger, my arm just feels so heavy, like I'm trying to lift it through water or something. And making breakfast? Forget about it. The other day I was just trying to make a piece of toast, and getting the bread out of the bag, putting it in the toaster, pushing the little lever down... it all took so much effort. I felt like I was moving so slowly that I actually stopped and just leaned against the counter for a minute because my arms felt so exhausted from just doing that. 

Even washing my own hair in the shower, which is ridiculous because I wash people's hair all day long, but lifting my arms up to scrub my own scalp just feels impossible. I have to keep taking breaks and putting my arms down because they just feel so weighed down and slow. It's like my whole body is just... lagging, you know? Like a computer that's taking too long to load. So yeah, it's definitely not just when I'm at work doing hair, it's creeping into literally everything I do at home, too, and it's just making everyday life feel like this huge, exhausting chore.
Have you been feeling sad, anxious, or depressed lately?

Yeah... yeah, I have. It's actually been really bad. I mean, most days I wake up and there's just this... this heavy, flat sadness right in the middle of my chest. It's not even like a sharp, crying kind of sad all the time, it's just this dead weight. Like, I'll open my eyes and immediately feel like there's no point in even trying to get out of bed, let alone trying to build the life I was planning. 

I was so excited when I got my associate's degree and got my license, you know? I had all these plans to build up my clientele, maybe open my own little studio suite eventually, take all these advanced color correction classes... and now? Now I just wake up and feel like... what's the point? It all just feels so hollow. I'll lie there looking at the ceiling and think about going to the salon, and instead of feeling motivated or even just normal about going to work, I just feel this overwhelming sense of dread and emptiness. It's like someone just came and sucked all the color out of my life, which is ironic since I literally do hair color for a living. 

But it's true, everything just feels gray and pointless. Even things that used to make me happy, like hanging out with my coworkers in the breakroom or watching my favorite shows when I get home... I just don't care anymore. I just feel so incredibly down, and it's there almost every single day. It's like this dark cloud that just settled over me and won't lift, no matter what I do, and it just makes all those plans I had for my future seem completely impossible and stupid.
Do you still enjoy activities that you used to find pleasurable before you started feeling this way?

Um... no, not really. I mean, not at all, honestly. Like I was saying, I used to be so different. At the salon, I was always the one talking, you know? I’d be chatting with my clients the whole time they were in my chair, asking about their kids, their vacations, whatever. And I loved it! I loved connecting with people. I’d even go out of my way to help the newer stylists if they were struggling with a formulation or a difficult cut, just because I enjoyed being involved and being part of the team. But now... now I just kind of keep my head down. I’ll barely say a word to my clients unless I absolutely have to, just the bare minimum about their hair, and then I just focus on getting it done so they can leave. 

And it’s the same outside of work, too. I used to go hiking with my friends almost every weekend. We’d pick a new trail, pack a lunch, make a whole day of it. I loved being outside, the fresh air, just laughing and catching up. But the last few times they asked me to go, I just made up some excuse about being tired or having errands to run, because the thought of actually going... it’s just too much. I don’t want to be around anyone. I just avoid people altogether now. It’s like... I just don’t have that spark in me anymore, you know? That thing that used to make me want to talk and do things and just be around people... it’s completely gone. I just want to be left alone, which is so weird for me, because I was never like that before all of this started.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless about things?

Yeah... yeah, I do. All the time, actually. It's... it's just this constant loop in my head, you know? Like, I just keep thinking about how I'm such a burden on everyone around me. My family, my coworkers... I mean, I can't even keep my basic responsibilities together at the salon anymore. I used to be the one who was always on top of everything, making sure the color bowls were washed, sweeping up between clients without even being asked, helping with inventory... and now I can barely even lift my arms to do a basic root touch-up. And I just think... I deserve this. I deserve feeling this miserable because I couldn't even keep my job together. 

And my money... oh my god, I used to be so good at saving. I was putting money away for that studio suite I wanted, and now I've just blown through so much of it because I'll call out sick and miss out on tips, or I'll just order takeout every single night because I'm too exhausted to cook, and it all just adds up. And then I sit there looking at my bank account and I just feel so incredibly worthless. Like, what kind of person just throws away everything they worked so hard for? I just feel like I'm failing at literally everything—my job, my finances, just being a normal person. It's like I'm dragging everyone else down with me, and I just can't shake this feeling that it's all my fault and I deserve exactly what's happening to me. It's just... it's so heavy, you know? Carrying that around all day.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life?

I mean... no, I don't have a plan or anything. I'm not sitting at home figuring out how to do it or looking for ways to actually hurt myself. But... honestly? Yeah, I do think about it. Not like actively *killing* myself, but just... just not being here anymore. 

Like, when I go to sleep at night, after I've spent the whole day just dragging myself around, ignoring my friends' texts, and feeling terrible about the money I'm wasting... I just lie there in the dark and think, man, it would just be so much easier if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. Because then, you know, nobody would have to deal with me anymore. My mom wouldn't have to worry about why I'm not calling her back, my manager at the salon wouldn't have to stress about me calling out sick or staring blankly at the wall in the breakroom, and I wouldn't have to keep feeling this heavy, awful guilt all the time. 

It just feels like it would solve everyone's problems, mine included, if I just went to sleep and that was it. Just... peaceful, you know? Blank. No more letting people down, no more feeling like a total failure because I can't even do a simple haircut without wanting to cry. So, no, I wouldn't ever actually *do* something to hurt myself, I really wouldn't, I don't have a plan or anything like that... but the thought of just slipping away and not waking up? Yeah, that thought is there a lot. It's actually kind of comforting in a really messed up way, just imagining that I wouldn't have to try so hard anymore and nobody would have to carry my dead weight.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, the heavy depression, this... this awful, suffocating feeling where I just can't function and everything feels so pointless? It's been with me for about a year and two months now. I remember because it started right around the time the salon was doing all the holiday promos last year, which is usually my favorite time, you know? The salon gets so busy, everyone's getting their hair done for parties, and usually, I thrive in that chaos. I love the energy, the music playing, helping people figure out their holiday looks. But last year, right around November, I just started feeling this... this drag. 

At first, I just thought I was burned out, because, you know, being a hairstylist, you're on your feet all day, your arms are always elevated, you're constantly talking, and the holidays are just non-stop. So I thought, okay, I'm just tired, I just need to get through December and then I can rest in January. But then January came, and I didn't bounce back. I actually felt worse. And then February hit, and it just kept spiraling down, deeper and deeper. 

And it's weird because I can track it almost perfectly by how my station looked. I used to keep my station immaculate—my shears wiped down, my clips organized by size, my products lined up perfectly with the labels facing out. But by the time we hit the spring, my station was just a disaster area, and I didn't even care. And then the summer came, and I stopped wanting to go outside altogether, which, like I said, I used to love hiking. And now here we are, a whole year and two months later, and it just hasn't lifted. It's just been this constant, heavy blanket over me for fourteen straight months, and it just feels like it's never going to end. I keep waiting to wake up and feel like my old self, but it's just... it's just been this same awful feeling day in and day out for over a year now.
Do you still find pleasure in any activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy before you started feeling this way?

No... no, not really. I mean, I try, sometimes I'll try to do the things I used to like, but it's just... it's like all the color is drained out of everything. It's so strange because I used to be such a social person. Like, at the salon, I was the one who was always chatting up my clients, you know? I knew everything about their lives, their kids, their vacations, and I actually cared. I loved talking to them. And I'd always be the one helping the newer stylists, too. Like, if an assistant was struggling with a foil placement or trying to figure out a toner formulation, I'd jump right in. I loved that feeling of connection, of being part of a team and just... being around people. 

But now? Now I just... I keep my head down. When I'm actually at work, which is hard enough, I just try to get through the appointment with as little talking as possible. I don't ask about their weekends, I don't make eye contact in the mirror unless I have to check the cut, I just... I just want them to leave so I can go sit in the back room by myself. It's like I don't have that spark in me anymore to even pretend to care. 

And it's not just work, either. Outside of work, I used to go hiking with my friends all the time. We had this whole group, and on Sundays, we'd pick a new trail, pack snacks, spend hours out in the sun... I loved being outside. I loved the fresh air and just laughing with everyone. But now, if they text me to go, I just make up an excuse or I just don't reply at all. I avoid them. I avoid everyone. The thought of having to put on hiking boots and go out there and try to make conversation and smile and act like I'm having fun... it just sounds exhausting. It's like my battery is at zero percent all the time, and I just don't have anything left to give to the things that used to make me happy. It's all just... flat. Everything is just flat and gray, and I just want to be left alone.
Have you experienced any unusual thoughts or heard any voices that others can't hear?

I mean... yeah. Actually, yes, I have. And it's really been freaking me out, honestly. It's so hard to even talk about because it sounds crazy, but... it happens a lot at work. 

You know, at the salon, there's always this constant upkeep. Sweeping is like a never-ending thing, you're always sweeping hair, and I usually do it when it's quiet or when my client is processing under the dryer. And we have this back area where the shampoo bowls are, which is kind of separated from the main cutting floor by this little half-wall, so it's usually a bit more peaceful back there. But lately, when I'm back there... especially when I'm sweeping up around the chairs or standing at the sink rinsing out the color bowls—which is this whole messy process because the color gets stuck in the plastic grooves and you really have to scrub them—I've been hearing... a voice. 

It's a woman's voice. The first time it happened, I totally thought it was one of the senior stylists, maybe Jessica or one of the front desk girls, standing just on the other side of the wall. Because it sounded so incredibly real, like she was standing right next to my shoulder. But she was saying... she was saying that I'm ruining everything. Just in this really mean, disappointed tone. Telling me I'm ruining everything. 

And I remember I actually dropped the tint brush I was holding and walked around the half-wall to see who it was, ready to just apologize or figure out what I did wrong, but... nobody was there. Like, nobody was even close by. The closest person was all the way up at the reception desk taking a phone call. And it keeps happening. Sometimes it even happens when I'm the last one closing up and the salon is literally, completely empty. The front doors are locked, the main lights are off, it's just me and the broom, and I'll hear her right behind me by the shampoo stations. Just telling me I'm ruining everything. 

It makes me freeze completely. I'll just stand there with the broom handle, or with my hands deep in the soapy water in the sink, just terrified to turn around. Because how can a woman be talking to me when I'm the only person in the entire building? I've actually gone and checked the bathrooms and the back supply closet just to make sure someone didn't sneak in or hide back there, because it sounds that clear. But it's always empty. It's just me. And I don't know who she is or why she's saying it, but it just adds to that whole heavy feeling I was telling you about, making me feel like I really am just messing up everyone's lives, even though I know logically there's nobody actually standing there.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since you started feeling this way?

Sleep is a whole other mess, but with food... yeah, my appetite is just completely gone. And it's not even like I'm purposely trying to diet or anything, because I'm definitely not. It's just... I'll get to the salon, right? And usually, I'd grab a bagel or a muffin from the bakery next door before my first client, and we have this little break room in the back with a mini-fridge where we'd all sit and eat lunch together between color processing times. I used to love lunch breaks. 

But lately, I just don't even think about food. I'll make a coffee when I get in—just a black coffee from the Keurig we have by the sink—and I'll just sip on that. And then the day just drags on, and I'm just trying to survive my appointments, just trying to push through that heavy feeling and ignore everything else. And then I'll get in my car to drive home at like seven or eight at night, and I'll realize... I've been skipping meals all day without really meaning to. It'll hit me right then that I only had that coffee and maybe a few bites of a stale granola bar I found at the bottom of my purse, and that's literally it for the entire day. I just have zero desire to eat, it's like my stomach doesn't even send signals to my brain anymore. 

And because of it, my clothes have gotten so much looser. Like, my favorite black work pants that used to fit perfectly and looked so professional? They're just hanging off me now. I have to keep pulling them up while I'm trying to cut hair, which is so annoying when you have shears in one hand and a comb in the other. Even my aprons feel huge. Everything just feels baggy and wrong on me now, but I just... I can't bring myself to care enough to actually sit down and make a real meal.
Have you experienced any periods of improvement in your mood or functioning since this heavy feeling started over a year ago?

I mean... if I really sit down and look back at the whole timeline, like over this entire past year or however long it's been since everything really started going downhill... it's mostly just been that same awful, heavy feeling. Like, I have spent the vast majority of this whole decline just feeling completely depressed and weighed down. It's like wearing a lead apron, you know? Like the heavy ones they put on you at the dentist to take x-rays, but I'm wearing it all the time, every single day. 

There were maybe a few little blips, I guess. Like, really short stretches where the sadness wasn't quite as prominent. I remember back in the spring, there was maybe a week, or maybe just a few days, where I thought, "Okay, maybe I'm finally snapping out of it." We had this huge bridal party come into the salon, and usually, those are so chaotic with the updos and the tight schedules and everyone running around with hot tools and hairspray just choking the air... but for a couple of days around then, I actually felt a little bit lighter. The gray cloud lifted just a tiny bit, and I could almost smile at the bride without having to force it so hard. I actually thought I was getting better. I even went online on my lunch break and looked at buying a new pair of texturizing shears because I thought I was going to get back into taking advanced cutting classes again. 

But it just never lasts. It's like, I'll get this tiny little window where the sadness backs off just a fraction, and I think I can finally breathe and be normal again, but then before I even realize what's happening, the heavy feeling just crashes right back down on me. Sometimes it feels even harder than before, honestly. And then I'm right back to hiding by the shampoo bowls and ignoring my friends' texts. So yeah, if you look at the whole picture, almost all of it has just been me drowning in this... this flatness and this heavy depression, with only those really, really brief moments where it wasn't completely suffocating. It's just so frustrating because whenever I get those little breaks, I get my hopes up, but the heavy feeling always, always comes back and takes over my whole life again.
Have you noticed any changes in your physical activity level or restlessness since you started feeling this way?

I'm definitely not restless. Honestly, it's... it's the exact opposite. It’s almost like I’m stuck in slow motion. You know how when you have a nightmare and you’re trying to run away from something but your legs just won't work? It feels exactly like that, but in real life, all day long. Especially with my hands. My hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work. 

And in a salon, you have to be fast. Timing is literally everything. If you're doing a full head of foils, you have to get those last sections in quickly or the bottom is going to over-process and fry off while you're still working on the top. I used to be so quick with my foil weaving, but lately... like, even just sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever now. I'll be standing in the back room just staring at the color bowl, trying to mix the developer and the tint with that little whisk we use, and my arm just feels so incredibly heavy. It takes so much physical effort just to stir it. Or I'll be standing behind the chair with my clips, trying to part out the standard four quadrants on a client's head, and my fingers just fumble and drag. 

And it's getting bad because people have started noticing I’m just slower than I used to be. My manager pulled me aside on Tuesday—or maybe it was Wednesday, I don't know—but she asked if I was feeling sick because a basic root touch-up that usually takes me thirty-five minutes took me over an hour. Even my regular clients are starting to get antsy. I can see them in the mirror shifting around, checking their Apple watches, looking at the clock on the wall. And I want to speed up, I really do. I keep telling my brain, 'just go faster, just move,' but I just can't. My whole body just feels weighed down and sluggish, like every single movement requires this massive amount of energy that I just don't have.

Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions or thoughts besides the voice you mentioned, such as seeing things that others can't or having thoughts that feel like they're being controlled or inserted by someone else?

Seeing things? No, I definitely don't see anything that isn't there. But as far as unusual thoughts... I mean, I don't know if it's unusual or if it's just me finally putting the pieces together, because it's been driving me absolutely crazy lately. 

I know it sounds strange, like, I know if I just say it out loud to someone who doesn't work there it might sound weird, but I’m pretty sure someone at the salon has been watching my bookings and messing with my hours on purpose. We use this booking software on the iPad at the front desk, and technically the receptionists are the ones who are supposed to manage the appointments, but honestly, anyone can walk up and look at the schedule if the screen is unlocked. And I've just noticed this really, really specific pattern over the last few months. 

It always happens the exact same way. I'll be in the break room, right? And I'll be talking to one of the other stylists, maybe mentioning that things are a little tight and I really need to put away some extra cash this month, or that I'm trying to build up my savings account so I have a little bit of a safety net. Just normal talk. But then, I swear to you, the slow days seem to happen right after I talk about saving money. 

It’s never a coincidence. I’ll have a totally solid week booked out—like, maybe three full highlights, a couple of root touch-ups, regular haircuts—and then the second I mention needing the money, suddenly my schedule for the rest of the week is just completely gutted. Clients that I know for a fact were on the books will mysteriously get moved to someone else's column, or they'll just be canceled altogether. And I'll just be standing there at my station, looking at my empty column on the app, knowing that someone is doing it to me. It’s like someone is actively listening to my conversations and then going into the system to sabotage my paycheck just to keep me down. I keep running through everyone in my head, trying to figure out who has it out for me, because it’s just too perfectly timed to be an accident. It's just... it's exhausting trying to work when you know someone is secretly pulling the strings behind your back like that.
Have the voices or the thoughts of someone sabotaging your bookings at the salon ever told you to harm yourself or others?

Harm myself or others? No, no, definitely not others. I mean, whoever is messing with my schedule makes me incredibly frustrated, obviously, but I would never actually do anything to hurt them or anyone else at the salon. And the voice doesn't tell me to do anything like that either. 

But... as far as hurting myself... I mean... I don't have a plan to hurt myself. I really don't. I'm not sitting around trying to figure out how to actually do something like that. But it's just... when you feel this heavy all the time, and you're constantly exhausted just from trying to mix a bowl of color or stand behind the chair, and then on top of it you have people sneaking around ruining your paychecks... it just wears you down to absolutely nothing. 

Like, I'll get home after a ten-hour shift, my feet are throbbing because those black anti-fatigue mats we have to stand on do absolutely nothing, and I'll just collapse on my bed. I won't even take my shoes off or scrub the hair dye off my wrists. I just lie there in the dark. And that's when my brain just starts... sinking. And I get these thoughts. Not plans, just... thoughts. Like, I'll just be lying there thinking about how much easier it would be if I just went to sleep and didn't wake up. If I just didn't have to open my eyes and put on that heavy lead apron and do it all over again. 

Because it's not just me who is exhausted by this, you know? I know I'm dragging everyone else down too. My manager is annoyed with how slow I am, my clients are getting impatient, I'm ignoring my friends' texts... so I just think, if I didn't wake up tomorrow, then nobody would have to deal with me anymore. It would just solve the problem for everyone. They could just hire a new stylist who is fast and normal and doesn't ruin the vibe. But like I said, I'm not going to actually do anything to make that happen. I don't have a plan. I just... sometimes I just really wish I could just fade out and let everyone off the hook.
Are there any activities that you still find enjoyable or that bring you pleasure?

Enjoyable? Pleasure? I mean... honestly, no. Not really. It’s like all the color has just been completely drained out of everything I used to like doing. 

I used to be so different, you know? Like, back when I first started at the salon, I was the one who was always chatting up my clients. I knew all about their kids, their vacations, their divorces... I loved that part of the job. I’d be foiling hair and just talking a mile a minute, laughing, making them feel good. And I used to really enjoy helping out the newer stylists, too. We’d have these little huddles in the break room where I’d show them my tricks for getting a really clean balayage blend, or how to formulate a toner that wouldn't pull too warm. I actually looked forward to that. I felt like I had this... this energy, this spark. 

And outside of work, I was always doing something. My friends and I used to go hiking all the time. We’d drive up to the state park on Sundays, pack these ridiculous lunches, and just hike for hours. I loved the fresh air, the feeling of my muscles working, just being out in the sun. We had this one trail we called "The Gauntlet" because it was so steep, but the view at the top was amazing. I used to live for those Sundays. 

But now... now I just don't care about any of it. I don't even know where that person went. At work, I just keep my head down. I barely say a word to my clients anymore, which I know they hate, but I just don't have the energy to fake a smile or pretend to care about their neighbor's new dog. I just stare at the mirror and focus on getting the color on the hair so I can go hide in the back. And I definitely don't help the new girls. I avoid everyone. I just want to be left alone. 

And hiking? God, I haven't been hiking in months. My friends still text me in our group chat, asking if I want to go this weekend or that weekend, and I just leave them on read or make up some excuse about being scheduled for a double shift. The thought of putting on my hiking boots and driving out there... it just sounds so exhausting and pointless. There’s no spark anymore. There’s just... nothing. I don't enjoy the things I used to, and I definitely haven't found anything new that makes me feel good. I just go to work, drag myself through the day, and go home to lie in the dark. That's it. That's my whole life right now.
Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions or thoughts that feel unreal or detached from reality?

Unreal or detached? Um, no, not really. I mean, besides the schedule thing I was talking about—which, like I said, I know is actually happening because the proof is right there on the iPad—I don't have anything else like that going on. 

I don't feel like I'm floating outside my body or like the world is a simulation or whatever people say when they feel detached. It's actually the opposite, honestly. Everything feels entirely too real and just incredibly heavy. Like I'm hyper-aware of every single exhausting detail of my day, from the exact weight of the blow dryer in my hand to the exact tone of my manager's voice when she asks why I'm running behind. I'm very much stuck right here in reality, just... dragging myself through it. So, no, nothing else unusual like that. Just the voice and the people messing with my bookings. That's more than enough to deal with, honestly.
Have you experienced any other hallucinations, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot, outside of the voice at the salon?

Outside of the salon? No. No, I don't see things, like shadows or people who aren't there, and I don't hear anything when I'm at home in my apartment or driving my car. It's really just... it's just that one voice at work. 

And it's so specific, you know? It's not like a constant chatter or anything. It usually happens when I'm doing the really mindless grunt work, like when I'm in the back room rinsing out the color bowls. We use these black plastic Framar bowls and the color gets really caked on if you don't scrub them right away with the hot water, so I'll be standing there scrubbing, smelling the developer and the bleach, just trying to get the stains out... or I'll be out on the floor sweeping up. Sweeping is the worst because the hair just sticks to everything, especially the little tiny hairs from a men's clipper cut, so I'm just pushing the broom around, really focused on trying to get it all into the dustpan before my next client... and that's when I hear her. 

It's a woman's voice. And it always sounds like it's coming right from the shampoo stations. We have this row of four sinks in the back, past the drying chairs, and it's sort of separated by this half-wall so clients can relax while they get washed. I'll just hear this woman, clear as day, coming from over by the sinks, and she just tells me that I'm ruining everything. Just... "you're ruining everything." 

And it makes my stomach drop every single time, because I'll look over, or I'll actually drop my broom and walk around the half-wall to see who is talking about me, and there's no one there. Sometimes it happens when I'm the one closing and the salon is literally empty. Like, the front doors are locked, the neon open sign is turned off, the other stylists have all gone home, it's just me cleaning up, and I still hear her over by the shampoo bowls telling me I'm ruining it all. Even when the salon is totally empty or nobody is anywhere close by, she's there. It's just so exhausting because I'm already trying so hard just to drag myself through my shift, and then I have to deal with her, whoever she is, just criticizing me out of thin air. So, no, nothing at home, nothing visual. Just her.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your relationships with friends and family since you started feeling this way?

Friends? Yeah... I mean, I kind of brought up the hiking group chat earlier, but it's honestly worse than just leaving them on read now. They're actually getting annoyed with me. I’ve pulled away so much that they’ve stopped reaching out as often, which I guess is what I wanted, but it still feels terrible. I'm just completely isolating myself from anyone who actually cares about me. 

And it’s not just my close friends, either. I used to do this volunteer thing that I was really proud of. Every other Sunday morning, before the salon opened, I’d go down to the senior center—the one over on Elm Street—and give free haircuts to the residents. I used to love it. doctor.question: Have you experienced any periods of improvement in your mood or functioning since this heavy feeling started over a year ago?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2
target_item.manifestation: Looking back, I have spent most of this whole decline feeling depressed and weighed down, with only shorter stretches where the sadness was not as prominent.

patient.answer:
I mean... if I really sit down and look back at the whole timeline, like over this entire past year or however long it's been since everything really started going downhill... it's mostly just been that same awful, heavy feeling. Like, I have spent the vast majority of this whole decline just feeling completely depressed and weighed down. It's like wearing a lead apron, you know? Like the heavy ones they put on you at the dentist to take x-rays, but I'm wearing it all the time, every single day. 

There were maybe a few little blips, I guess. Like, really short stretches where the sadness wasn't quite as prominent. I remember back in the spring, there was maybe a week, or maybe just a few days, where I thought, "Okay, maybe I'm finally snapping out of it." We had this huge bridal party come into the salon, and usually, those are so chaotic with the updos and the tight schedules and everyone running around with hot tools and hairspray just choking the air... but for a couple of days around then, I actually felt a little bit lighter. The gray cloud lifted just a tiny bit, and I could almost smile at the bride without having to force it so hard. I actually thought I was getting better. I even went online on my lunch break and looked at buying a new pair of texturizing shears because I thought I was going to get back into taking advanced cutting classes again. 

But it just never lasts. It's like, I'll get this tiny little window where the sadness backs off just a fraction, and I think I can finally breathe and be normal again, but then before I even realize what's happening, the heavy feeling just crashes right back down on me. Sometimes it feels even harder than before, honestly. And then I'm right back to hiding by the shampoo bowls and ignoring my friends' texts. So yeah, if you look at the whole picture, almost all of it has just been me drowning in this... this flatness and this heavy depression, with only those really, really brief moments where it wasn't completely suffocating. It's just so frustrating because whenever I get those little breaks, I get my hopes up, but the heavy feeling always, always comes back and takes over my whole life again.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of psychomotor agitation or retardation

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: My hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work, like even sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever now, and people have started noticing I’m just slower than I used to be.

patient.answer:
I'm definitely not restless. Honestly, it's... it's the exact opposite. It’s almost like I’m stuck in slow motion. You know how when you have a nightmare and you’re trying to run away from something but your legs just won't work? It feels exactly like that, but in real life, all day long. Especially with my hands. My hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work. 

And in a salon, you have to be fast. Timing is literally everything. If you're doing a full head of foils, you have to get those last sections in quickly or the bottom is going to over-process and fry off while you're still working on the top. I used to be so quick with my foil weaving, but lately... like, even just sectioning hair or mixing color takes me forever now. I'll be standing in the back room just staring at the color bowl, trying to mix the developer and the tint with that little whisk we use, and my arm just feels so incredibly heavy. It takes so much physical effort just to stir it. Or I'll be standing behind the chair with my clips, trying to part out the standard four quadrants on a client's head, and my fingers just fumble and drag. 

And it's getting bad because people have started noticing I’m just slower than I used to be. My manager pulled me aside on Tuesday—or maybe it was Wednesday, I don't know—but she asked if I was feeling sick because a basic root touch-up that usually takes me thirty-five minutes took me over an hour. Even my regular clients are starting to get antsy. I can see them in the mirror shifting around, checking their Apple watches, looking at the clock on the wall. And I want to speed up, I really do. I keep telling my brain, 'just go faster, just move,' but I just can't. My whole body just feels weighed down and sluggish, like every single movement requires this massive amount of energy that I just don't have.

patient.answer:
Seeing things? No, I definitely don't see anything that isn't there. But as far as unusual thoughts... I mean, I don't know if it's unusual or if it's just me finally putting the pieces together, because it's been driving me absolutely crazy lately. 

I know it sounds strange, like, I know if I just say it out loud to someone who doesn't work there it might sound weird, but I’m pretty sure someone at the salon has been watching my bookings and messing with my hours on purpose. We use this booking software on the iPad at the front desk, and technically the receptionists are the ones who are supposed to manage the appointments, but honestly, anyone can walk up and look at the schedule if the screen is unlocked. And I've just noticed this really, really specific pattern over the last few months. 

It always happens the exact same way. I'll be in the break room, right? And I'll be talking to one of the other stylists, maybe mentioning that things are a little tight and I really need to put away some extra cash this month, or that I'm trying to build up my savings account so I have a little bit of a safety net. Just normal talk. But then, I swear to you, the slow days seem to happen right after I talk about saving money. 

It’s never a coincidence. I’ll have a totally solid week booked out—like, maybe three full highlights, a couple of root touch-ups, regular haircuts—and then the second I mention needing the money, suddenly my schedule for the rest of the week is just completely gutted. Clients that I know for a fact were on the books will mysteriously get moved to someone else's column, or they'll just be canceled altogether. And I'll just be standing there at my station, looking at my empty column on the app, knowing that someone is doing it to me. It’s like someone is actively listening to my conversations and then going into the system to sabotage my paycheck just to keep me down. I keep running through everyone in my head, trying to figure out who has it out for me, because it’s just too perfectly timed to be an accident. It's just... it's exhausting trying to work when you know someone is secretly pulling the strings behind your back like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's depression is severe enough to be considered major depressive disorder with psychotic features
doctor.question: Have the voices or the thoughts of someone sabotaging your bookings at the salon ever told you to harm yourself or others?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but I get thoughts like it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up and nobody had to deal with me anymore.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the voices or thoughts have instructed me to harm myself or others, which is an inquiry into suicidal or homicidal ideation, mapping to the Death_Suicide symptom.

patient.answer:
Harm myself or others? No, no, definitely not others. I mean, whoever is messing with my schedule makes me incredibly frustrated, obviously, but I would never actually do anything to hurt them or anyone else at the salon. And the voice doesn't tell me to do anything like that either. 

But... as far as hurting myself... I mean... I don't have a plan to hurt myself. I really don't. I'm not sitting around trying to figure out how to actually do something like that. But it's just... when you feel this heavy all the time, and you're constantly exhausted just from trying to mix a bowl of color or stand behind the chair, and then on top of it you have people sneaking around ruining your paychecks... it just wears you down to absolutely nothing. 

Like, I'll get home after a ten-hour shift, my feet are throbbing because those black anti-fatigue mats we have to stand on do absolutely nothing, and I'll just collapse on my bed. I won't even take my shoes off or scrub the hair dye off my wrists. I just lie there in the dark. And that's when my brain just starts... sinking. And I get these thoughts. Not plans, just... thoughts. Like, I'll just be lying there thinking about how much easier it would be if I just went to sleep and didn't wake up. If I just didn't have to open my eyes and put on that heavy lead apron and do it all over again. 

Because it's not just me who is exhausted by this, you know? I know I'm dragging everyone else down too. My manager is annoyed with how slow I am, my clients are getting impatient, I'm ignoring my friends' texts... so I just think, if I didn't wake up tomorrow, then nobody would have to deal with me anymore. It would just solve the problem for everyone. They could just hire a new stylist who is fast and normal and doesn't ruin the vibe. But like I said, I'm not going to actually do anything to make that happen. I don't have a plan. I just... sometimes I just really wish I could just fade out and let everyone off the hook.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of anhedonia
doctor.question: Are there any activities that you still find enjoyable or that bring you pleasure?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: I used to chat with clients, help the newer stylists, and go hiking with friends, but now I mostly keep my head down and avoid people because I just don’t have that spark in me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about anhedonia (loss of pleasure or interest in activities), which maps to the negative symptoms profile where the patient describes losing interest in previously enjoyed activities like hiking and socializing.

patient.answer:
Enjoyable? Pleasure? I mean... honestly, no. Not really. It’s like all the color has just been completely drained out of everything I used to like doing. 

I used to be so different, you know? Like, back when I first started at the salon, I was the one who was always chatting up my clients. I knew all about their kids, their vacations, their divorces... I loved that part of the job. I’d be foiling hair and just talking a mile a minute, laughing, making them feel good. And I used to really enjoy helping out the newer stylists, too. We’d have these little huddles in the break room where I’d show them my tricks for getting a really clean balayage blend, or how to formulate a toner that wouldn't pull too warm. I actually looked forward to that. I felt like I had this... this energy, this spark. 

And outside of work, I was always doing something. My friends and I used to go hiking all the time. We’d drive up to the state park on Sundays, pack these ridiculous lunches, and just hike for hours. I loved the fresh air, the feeling of my muscles working, just being out in the sun. We had this one trail we called "The Gauntlet" because it was so steep, but the view at the top was amazing. I used to live for those Sundays. 

But now... now I just don't care about any of it. I don't even know where that person went. At work, I just keep my head down. I barely say a word to my clients anymore, which I know they hate, but I just don't have the energy to fake a smile or pretend to care about their neighbor's new dog. I just stare at the mirror and focus on getting the color on the hair so I can go hide in the back. And I definitely don't help the new girls. I avoid everyone. I just want to be left alone. 

And hiking? God, I haven't been hiking in months. My friends still text me in our group chat, asking if I want to go this weekend or that weekend, and I just leave them on read or make up some excuse about being scheduled for a double shift. The thought of putting on my hiking boots and driving out there... it just sounds so exhausting and pointless. There’s no spark anymore. There’s just... nothing. I don't enjoy the things I used to, and I definitely haven't found anything new that makes me feel good. I just go to work, drag myself through the day, and go home to lie in the dark. That's it. That's my whole life right now.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of psychotic symptoms
doctor.question: Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions or thoughts that feel unreal or detached from reality?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about other unusual perceptions or thoughts (hallucinations or delusions). The patient has already discussed their auditory hallucinations (the voice) and delusions (sabotage), and does not have any other psychotic symptoms in their profile.

patient.answer:
Unreal or detached? Um, no, not really. I mean, besides the schedule thing I was talking about—which, like I said, I know is actually happening because the proof is right there on the iPad—I don't have anything else like that going on. 

I don't feel like I'm floating outside my body or like the world is a simulation or whatever people say when they feel detached. It's actually the opposite, honestly. Everything feels entirely too real and just incredibly heavy. Like I'm hyper-aware of every single exhausting detail of my day, from the exact weight of the blow dryer in my hand to the exact tone of my manager's voice when she asks why I'm running behind. I'm very much stuck right here in reality, just... dragging myself through it. So, no, nothing else unusual like that. Just the voice and the people messing with my bookings. That's more than enough to deal with, honestly.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of psychotic symptoms to differentiate between depressive disorders
doctor.question: Have you experienced any other hallucinations, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot, outside of the voice at the salon?

target_item.name: Hallucinations

patient.answer:
Outside of the salon? No. No, I don't see things, like shadows or people who aren't there, and I don't hear anything when I'm at home in my apartment or driving my car. It's really just... it's just that one voice at work. 

And it's so specific, you know? It's not like a constant chatter or anything. It usually happens when I'm doing the really mindless grunt work, like when I'm in the back room rinsing out the color bowls. We use these black plastic Framar bowls and the color gets really caked on if you don't scrub them right away with the hot water, so I'll be standing there scrubbing, smelling the developer and the bleach, just trying to get the stains out... or I'll be out on the floor sweeping up. Sweeping is the worst because the hair just sticks to everything, especially the little tiny hairs from a men's clipper cut, so I'm just pushing the broom around, really focused on trying to get it all into the dustpan before my next client... and that's when I hear her. 

It's a woman's voice. And it always sounds like it's coming right from the shampoo stations. We have this row of four sinks in the back, past the drying chairs, and it's sort of separated by this half-wall so clients can relax while they get washed. I'll just hear this woman, clear as day, coming from over by the sinks, and she just tells me that I'm ruining everything. Just... "you're ruining everything." 

And it makes my stomach drop every single time, because I'll look over, or I'll actually drop my broom and walk around the half-wall to see who is talking about me, and there's no one there. Sometimes it happens when I'm the one closing and the salon is literally empty. Like, the front doors are locked, the neon open sign is turned off, the other stylists have all gone home, it's just me cleaning up, and I still hear her over by the shampoo bowls telling me I'm ruining it all. Even when the salon is totally empty or nobody is anywhere close by, she's there. It's just so exhausting because I'm already trying so hard just to drag myself through my shift, and then I have to deal with her, whoever she is, just criticizing me out of thin air. So, no, nothing at home, nothing visual. Just her.

patient.answer:
Friends? Yeah... I mean, I kind of brought up the hiking group chat earlier, but it's honestly worse than just leaving them on read now. They're actually getting annoyed with me. I’ve pulled away so much that they’ve stopped reaching out as often, which I guess is what I wanted, but it still feels terrible. And it’s not just my close friends, either. I used to do this volunteer thing that I was really proud of. Every other Sunday morning, before the salon opened, I’d go down to the senior center—the one over on Elm Street—and give free haircuts to the residents. I used to love it. I'd do these little roller sets and basic trims for the older ladies, and they were always so sweet, telling me all about their grandkids. But I just... stopped showing up. I didn't even call the coordinator to explain or tell them I needed a break. I just completely ghosted them. The thought of packing up my shears and my combs and standing there trying to make polite conversation while doing a perm... I just couldn't do it anymore. I couldn't get out of bed. 

And that same thing is ruining my relationships at work, too. I have completely lost the trust of my manager and my clients. My manager, Sarah, she used to rely on me for everything. I was the one she’d ask to do the color inventory, or handle the closing drawer, but I've just been canceling on all the extra things I used to reliably handle for her. I'll call out sick, or I'll just tell her I can't do the inventory because I have a headache. 

And my clients... I mean, they don't trust me anymore either, and I don't blame them. I keep making all these stupid mistakes with really basic salon routines. Like, things I could do in my sleep a year ago. Last week, I completely messed up a simple root smudge because I grabbed a 20-volume developer instead of a 10-volume, and it lifted the client's base instead of just depositing the tone. It was a disaster. Sarah had to step in and fix it. And I just work so incredibly slowly now. A standard cut and blowout used to take me forty-five minutes, tops, but now I'm dragging it out to an hour and a half because I just move like I'm underwater. I'll just stand there holding a section of hair, staring blankly at the mirror, trying to gather the energy to pick up the round brush. My clients look at their watches, they sigh, they get visibly irritated... a lot of my regulars have actually stopped rebooking with me and are going to the other girls instead. So yeah, I'm pretty much just letting absolutely everyone down right now.

That all just feels so far away and impossible. The motivation is just totally gone, completely replaced by that heavy, flat feeling in my chest. So, yeah, getting out of bed is a massive struggle, and there are definitely stretches of days where I just don't do it at all unless I am absolutely forced to.
